evidence: paper: \tau = 1 - t, \qquad A = \tfrac12 + h, \qquad D = \tfrac12 - h, \qquad 0 < h < 1/100,

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. A = 1/2 + h and D = 1/2 - h are literal definition bodies (CoordinateAlgebra.A/D, duplicated verbatim as NaturalAxisData.A/D). τ = 1 - t is not a named definition: the substitution 1 - p.1 is written into the coordinate itself (SimilarityProfile.q), and the docstring of SimilarityCoordinates.coordinateQ_hasDerivAt_time says 'the physical time is t = 1 - τ'. The range 0 < h < 1/100 is the printed range of NaturalAxisRange.Parameters, but with ≤ 1/100 rather than <; strictness holds for the exponent actually used (selected_exponent_small, derived from the tighter h ≤ 1/1000 of NaturalAxisData.SmallParameters). The coordinate lemmas of SimilarityCoordinates / SimilarityProfile assume only 0 < h < 1/2, a weaker hypothesis than the paper's.
